_doc: CHARPANEL: the FIELD-SCOPED Character-panel apply law, pinned across the
three LIVE implementations (the workspace_interpreter reference, Rust
jas_dioxus, Swift JasSwift). See transcripts/CHARACTER.md
'The field-scoped apply law'.
THE LAW. A Character-panel edit names the field the user just committed.
Only the attribute GROUP that field owns is taken from panel state; every
other character attribute is preserved from the element being edited, per
element. The old law rebuilt the WHOLE attribute set from panel state on
every edit, so nudging Tracking on a 30pt bold italic underlined Georgia
run reset it to the panel's 12pt sans-serif defaults - sixteen attributes
clobbered by one edit (JYH, banked in transcripts/STROKE.md follow-ups
during STROKEWIDTH). Vector 'tracking_edit_preserves_the_rich_run' is that
exact repro and FAILS under the old law (it yields font_family
'sans-serif', not 'Georgia').
THE GROUPS. font_family->font_family; style_name->the font_weight +
font_style PAIR (one dropdown names both, and an unrecognised name writes
NEITHER); font_size->font_size ONLY (never line_height: Auto leading is an
ABSENT line-height, so preserving it keeps Auto alive and lets it
re-derive against the new size); leading->line_height; kerning->kerning;
tracking->letter_spacing; vertical_scale->vertical_scale ONLY and
horizontal_scale->horizontal_scale ONLY (two independent inputs, so each
is its own group - grouping them would let one edit stamp the panel's
value for the other, the mistake the Stroke law's two arrowhead scales
already paid for); baseline_shift / superscript / subscript -> the single
baseline_shift attribute, toggles winning over the number;
character_rotation->rotate; all_caps and small_caps -> the text_transform
+ font_variant PAIR (their mutual exclusion cannot be expressed one
attribute at a time: turning All Caps ON must clear a small-caps
font_variant); underline and strikethrough -> the whole text_decoration
token list (a CSS token list cannot be written a token at a time, exactly
as a dash array cannot be written a slot at a time); language->xml_lang;
THE SIBLING RULE. Three groups are fed by more than one panel FIELD:
DECORATION (underline + strikethrough), CASE (all_caps + small_caps) and
BASELINE_SHIFT (baseline_shift + superscript + subscript). For those, the
committed field is read from PANEL STATE and every SIBLING field is read
from the ELEMENT being edited - never from panel state, which the law does
not guarantee has been mirrored from the selection. (Before CHARPANEL's
repair only Swift's panel VIEW pushed such a mirror, so the ports read
different data and Rust destroyed the sibling's attribute: element
line-through + Underline clicked wrote a bare 'underline'.) Where the
committed field and an element-read sibling conflict, the COMMITTED field
wins - it is the one the user just chose. The one exception is a numeric
field at its identity: committing 0 into Baseline Shift carries no intent
(0 is what the input displays while super / sub is set), so the element's
super / sub stands. Vectors whose _comment says STALE-SIBLING
DISCRIMINATOR fail against a law that reads siblings from panel state;
the reference arm asserts that rejection, and every multi-field-group
vector's 'panel' delta names at most its own 'edited' field so no vector
can go green on a mirrored sibling it was handed.
anti_aliasing->aa_mode. Every other panel field owns no element attribute
and writes NOTHING - the seven snap_* flags and the section-visibility
flags are UI-only state, and toggling one must not push an undo step that
changes nothing.
SHAPE. Each vector is language-neutral. 'op' is always 'panel_edit'.
'edited' is the committed panel field key; unlike the Stroke panel there
is no flat-global spelling to normalize, because every Character control
binds panel.<field> only (workspace/panels/character.yaml). 'base' is the
element's existing character state as a flat attribute map, or the string
'rich_run' naming the shared map below; it is itself a DELTA over
'element_defaults'. 'panel' is a DELTA over 'panel_defaults' below - only
the fields the vector cares about. 'expected' is likewise a DELTA merged
over the effective base: the keys it names are what the edit CHANGED, and
every key it omits must come back unchanged. That is the whole point of
the law, so the delta form states it directly. An 'expected' of {} means
the edit wrote nothing that differs; an 'expected' of null means NO WRITE
REACHES THE DOCUMENT AT ALL (no undo step, element untouched).
ATTRIBUTE NAMES are the element's SVG / CSS attributes per CHARACTER.md's
mapping table, not panel field names: the panel's 'leading' field writes
line_height, its 'tracking' field writes letter_spacing, and its
'style_name' dropdown writes font_weight + font_style. Empty string is
the identity value for every string attribute (CHARACTER.md's
identity-omission rule: a default is stored as absence).

element_defaults._comment: A plain 12pt element: every attribute at its identity value. Each port builds its Text / TextPath from this map merged with the vector's 'base', so no port's constructor defaults leak into the corpus.

panel_defaults._comment: The Character panel sitting at the defaults workspace/panels/character.yaml declares - the state that used to be stamped over the whole selection on every edit.

rich_run._comment: JYH's repro element: a deliberately rich 30pt run where EVERY attribute differs from the panel defaults, so any whole-rebuild shows up as a diff. text_transform is uppercase with an empty font_variant because All Caps and Small Caps are mutually exclusive - the small-caps side is exercised by its own base.

vectors.name: tracking_edit_preserves_the_rich_run
vectors._comment: JYH's EXACT repro. Rich 30pt run selected, panel at its 12pt defaults, user commits Tracking = 50. Only letter_spacing changes. Under the old whole-rebuild law all sixteen attributes came back at the panel defaults (font_family 'sans-serif', font_size 12, normal/normal, no decoration, no caps, no shift, Auto leading, no lang, no aa, no rotation, identity scales, no kerning) - this vector is the RED one.

vectors.name: font_size_edit_writes_only_the_size
vectors._comment: The rich run carries an EXPLICIT line_height of 40pt. A size edit must leave it alone - the leading is the user's, not a function of the size.

vectors.name: font_size_edit_preserves_auto_leading
vectors._comment: Auto leading is an ABSENT line-height. Because font_size owns ONLY font_size, the empty attribute survives and Auto re-derives against the new size (18 x 1.2 = 21.6) with no post-write hook bumping the panel's leading in step. The whole-rebuild law needed that hook; the field-scoped law does not.

vectors.name: style_edit_writes_the_weight_and_style_pair
vectors._comment: The rich run is bold italic; the panel's Regular writes BOTH normal/normal. One dropdown, one pair - there is no control that moves the weight without the style.

vectors.name: unknown_style_name_writes_neither_attribute
vectors._comment: An unrecognised Style entry leaves BOTH the weight and the style alone rather than guessing one half of the pair. Expected is the EMPTY delta: the write reaches the element and changes nothing.

vectors.name: leading_at_the_element_auto_ratio_restores_auto
vectors._comment: THE RULING: Auto is tested against the ELEMENT's font size, not the panel's. The rich run is 30pt, so a leading of 36 is exactly its Auto value and the attribute goes back to empty - even though the panel's own font_size field sits at the 12pt default (whose Auto value would be 14.4). Under the field-scoped law a leading edit must not consult a font-size field the user did not touch.

vectors.name: horizontal_scale_edit_leaves_the_vertical_scale
vectors._comment: The two scales are SEPARATE groups. The panel's vertical_scale sits at the 100 default while the element's is 90; a horizontal edit must not stamp the identity over it.

vectors.name: superscript_toggle_wins_over_the_elements_number
vectors._comment: Three FIELDS share the one baseline_shift attribute, so the two the user did NOT commit are read from the ELEMENT: the element carries a 4pt numeric shift and the committed Superscript toggle overrides it. The panel names only the committed field - it is under no obligation to have mirrored the other two.

vectors.name: subscript_on_replaces_a_superscript
vectors._comment: The COMMITTED field wins over its exclusion siblings: the element is superscript, the user commits Subscript, sub lands. The element-read sibling decides only what happens to the fields the user did NOT touch.

vectors.name: superscript_off_keeps_the_elements_numeric_shift
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR. Turning Superscript off on an element carrying a 4pt shift must leave the 4pt alone, because the number is read from the ELEMENT. A law that read the panel's number instead finds its 0.0 default and destroys the shift - which is what the ports did before CHARPANEL's repair.

vectors.name: superscript_off_keeps_the_elements_subscript
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR, one sibling over: the element is subscript, the user turns Superscript off, and sub survives.

vectors.name: a_zero_number_defers_to_the_elements_superscript
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR, and the ruling that resolves number-vs-toggle precedence under field scoping: 0 is exactly what the numeric input DISPLAYS while super / sub is set, so committing 0 carries no intent and the element's superscript stands. An explicit non-zero number does replace it (next vector).

vectors.name: all_caps_on_clears_a_small_caps_variant
vectors._comment: Why CASE is a two-attribute group: the element is small-caps, the user turns All Caps ON, and the exclusion rule requires text_transform AND font_variant to move together. A one-attribute write could not clear the variant. The panel names ONLY all_caps; the small-caps sibling is read from the element.

vectors.name: all_caps_off_keeps_a_small_caps_variant
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR. The element is small-caps with no transform; turning All Caps off must leave the variant alone. A law that read the panel's small_caps finds its false default and clears it.

vectors.name: small_caps_on_replaces_the_all_caps
vectors._comment: The COMMITTED field wins over its exclusion sibling: the element is uppercase, the user commits Small Caps, the transform clears and the variant lands. This is the vector the two ports disagreed on before CHARPANEL's repair - Swift's view mirror let the element's All Caps win and the click no-oped, Rust honoured the click. The click wins.

vectors.name: small_caps_off_keeps_the_all_caps
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR. Turning Small Caps off on an uppercase element must leave the uppercase: all_caps is read from the ELEMENT. A law that read the panel's all_caps finds its false default and destroys the transform.

vectors.name: underline_edit_rewrites_the_whole_decoration_list
vectors._comment: Why DECORATION is one group: two toggles feed ONE CSS token list, which cannot be written a token at a time. STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR: the panel names only underline (its strikethrough flag sits at the false default) and the line-through survives because the SIBLING flag is read from the element. Alphabetical order, so equality never depends on which toggle the user hit first.

vectors.name: underline_off_keeps_the_strikethrough
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR. Un-underlining must not un-strike.

vectors.name: strikethrough_edit_writes_the_decoration
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR the other way round: the element is underlined, the panel's underline flag sits at false, and committing Strikethrough must ADD to the list rather than replace it.

vectors.name: strikethrough_off_keeps_the_underline
vectors._comment: STALE-SIBLING DISCRIMINATOR. Un-striking must not un-underline.

vectors.name: snap_baseline_toggle_writes_nothing
vectors._comment: A UI-only flag owns no element attribute, so the edit must not reach the document at all - not even an undo step that changes nothing. Under the old law it re-stamped the entire panel over the selection.
